<details>
<summary>[ ] Scene</summary>

The trees thin out and the ground underfoot goes hard. Dark stone covers the clearing in a wide flat sheet — rough on top, cracked where it meets the soil at the edges. It stretches from the tree line to the cliff wall ahead where a dark opening gapes in the rock face. Bones and dried blood stain the ground in front of it.

</details>

---
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. Cracked bones litter the ground — leg bones, ribs, some large. The blood is old, dark brown, layered thick. The opening drops steeply into darkness. Inside, the walls are smooth to the touch — no chisel marks, no seams.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. The passage drops at a steep angle, straight as an arrow, wide enough for three abreast. The air gets warmer the deeper you go. At the bottom, three tunnels branch from a junction — left, right, and straight ahead.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. Climbs up and to the left. Opens into a round room. Every step crunches — the floor is bone, crushed fine. A few piles of intact pieces sit against the walls. Dull metallic veins catch torchlight in the exposed rock.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. Drops down and to the left. The smell hits three steps in. The floor is caked in droppings — thick, layered, with bone chips pressed into it. Dull metallic veins in the walls here too.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. Climbs up and to the right into the largest space. A thick stone pillar holds the ceiling at the center, open floor all around it. Brown dead moss covers the ground wall to wall. Three alcoves cut into the walls — two on the right, one on the left. Dull metallic veins here as well.
    1. Something large and low shifts in the moss ahead. *[Cackler Matriarch + pack. Link: Cackler Matriarch, Cacklers bestiary entries.]*
    2. One alcove holds a pile of meat — the sharp sting of ammonia comes off it. From another, small shapes press back against the stone, whimpering.

</details>

---

| Destination | Biome | Path Type | 
| --- | --- | --- | 
| Timber Knot Hovel | Deep Amber | Anaconda Path | 
| The Big Hill | Amberwood | Game Trail | 

---

Ork strip mine. The orks melted stone to bore the tunnels — no supports needed because the walls are fused solid. Beasts of burden dragged sleds of molten rock to the surface where it was poured out to cool, creating the dark stone apron outside the entrance. The orks extracted the densest ores and left. The remaining metallic veins in all three rooms past the junction are still valuable — players just need a sample.

A cackler pack has taken over the main chamber. The matriarch nests here with pups in one of the alcoves. The crushed bone room is the feeding floor. The right chamber is the latrine. The dead moss was surface material hauled underground to line the nest. If the party kills the matriarch and pack, the pups remain.

description:
*First visited: Expedition #*
- [ ] **Visit 1**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Scene</summary>

A hexagonal stone tower rises from the base of a cliff wall. It's tall — taller than anything else in the valley. Six massive pillars hold the base of the tower off the ground. In the gaps between the pillars, stone figures move. Some carry blocks. Others press them into place with wet mortar. The sound of grinding stone carries across the distance.

</details>

<details>
<summary>[ ] Callouts</summary>

The tower is not ruined. It looks new.

The figures at the base move with purpose — slow, deliberate, mechanical.

The gaps between the pillars are being filled in with fresh blocks.

Larger figures stand watch near the workers. They don't move unless something approaches.

A wide entrance at ground level, dark inside.

</details>
- [ ] **Visit 2 (Progressive)**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Scene</summary>

(The pillar gaps are more filled in. The tower is visibly taller. More figures working.)

</details>
- [ ] **Visit 3 (Progressive)**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Scene</summary>

(Construction nearly complete at this level. The tower may begin lifting again soon.)

</details>

---
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. The space beneath the raised tower. Six stone pillars hold the structure up. Fresh blocks fill most of the gaps. Stone figures carry blocks from small lifts and press them into place.
    1. The figures ignore anything that stays outside the pillar perimeter.
    2. Larger figures with shields stand at the gaps that aren't yet filled. They face outward.
    3. **Intuition (2):** The blocks are unnaturally uniform — smooth, dark, cast rather than carved.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. A wide hexagonal doorway at ground level. No door — just an open passage into darkness. The air inside is hot.
    1. The floor is smooth stone. Grooves run along the walls in straight lines.
    2. In the center of the room, a large stone platform sits flush with the floor. It doesn't move.
    3. **Intellect (3):** The platform is mechanical. It's locked in place — whatever activates it isn't here.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. One floor up via a spiral staircase that hugs the hexagonal wall. The stairs exit on the opposite side of the room from where they began. The heat is stronger here. Stone figures stand in alcoves along the walls.
    1. The figures activate when a living creature enters the room.
    2. The floor vibrates faintly. A deep rhythmic sound comes from above.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. The stairs cross to the opposite wall and climb to a room that glows orange. Stone channels in the floor carry molten rock from pipes in the wall. Molds line the far wall — rectangular, uniform. The heat is intense.
    1. Finished blocks cool in rows near a small lift shaft. The blocks are dark and smooth.
    2. **Fortitude (3):** Extended time in this room without protection causes heat exhaustion.
    3. **Intellect (3):** The molds produce identical blocks. The molten rock comes from deep below through the same pipe system that feeds the floor above.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. The entire floor is a single massive mechanism. Pistons, gears, and pipes fill the space from wall to wall. Steam vents hiss at irregular intervals. The rhythmic sound from below is deafening here.
    1. Pipes run downward through the floor and upward through the ceiling. Some carry heat. Others carry water.
    2. Smaller tubes run along the walls — too small for a person, pressurized, with objects moving inside them.
    3. **Intellect (4):** This is the heart of the structure. It powers the lifting mechanism, the foundry, and a distribution system that sends small objects throughout the tower.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. Racks of small glowing objects line the walls. Pneumatic tubes terminate here from every direction. Some racks hold objects that glow bright. Others hold dim or dark ones.
    1. A mechanism in the center of the room accepts dark objects from incoming tubes and places them onto a heating element. After a time, they glow again and are loaded into outgoing tubes.
    2. **Intellect (3):** These are power sources. Spent ones come in, get recharged by the heat from below, and get sent back out.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. Small lift shafts open on every wall. Stone figures load and unload materials — blocks, parts, raw metal. A constant flow of movement between the lifts and staging areas.
    1. The figures here are smaller and faster than the ones outside. They ignore intruders unless blocked.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. Shelves and bins fill the floor. Raw metal ingots, cast components, and materials sorted by type and size. Neat, organized, untouched by time.
    1. **Intellect (2):** The metal is unfamiliar — not iron, not copper. Something else.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. Crucibles and furnaces line the walls. Raw ore enters from below via small lifts. Refined metal exits upward. The air smells sharp and metallic.
    1. The process is automated. Stone figures tend the furnaces without pause.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. Workbenches and precision tools. Partially assembled components sit in organized rows — limbs, joints, housings, mechanisms. Everything scaled to the size of the stone figures.
    1. **Intellect (4):** These are parts for constructing new figures. The designs are identical — standardized production.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. The largest open floor in the tower. Assembly frames hold figures in various stages of completion. Tools, materials, and components surround each frame. One figure stands at the center of the room — larger than any other in the tower, unmoving, watching.
    1. The large figure does not activate until approached or until the assembly process is interfered with.
    2. **Intuition (3):** This one is different from the others. It moves its head to track you.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. A clean, quiet room after the noise below. A stone table dominates the center with channels carved into its surface. Small objects rest in some channels. The walls have slots and levers.
    1. **Intellect (5):** This is the control room. The table is a map or status display of the tower's systems. The levers control functions — including the elevator lock.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. Open sky. The top of the tower is flat and unfinished — fresh mortar, stacked blocks, tools. The view stretches across the valley. Wind up here is strong.
    1. The cliff wall is an arm's reach away. Raw stone face, no workings.
    2. The height is dizzying. Everything below is small.

</details>

---

| Destination | Biome | Path Type | 
| --- | --- | --- | 
| The Verdant Watch | Deep Amber | Bushwhack | 

---

**Ancient Dwarven Elevator Tower.** A fully functional piece of pre-war Dwarven infrastructure. The elevator descends far below the surface — destination unknown at this stage. The elevator is locked and cannot be activated until the Command floor is accessed and the lock is released.

**Self-expanding.** The tower grows itself. The entire structure lifts upward on internal tracks, creating a gap at the base. The Foundry casts lava into uniform basalt blocks. Hauling sentries deliver blocks via internal lifts to construction sentries at the expansion zone, who fill in the gap with fresh blocks and mortar. The tower is taller every time players visit.

**Floor layout (bottom to top):**

Elevator / Entrance → Security → Foundry → Engine Room → Core Exchange → Delivery → Storage → Refinery → Engineering → Manufactory (boss) → Command → Roof

**Power system.** Lava and water are piped up from deep below. The Engine Room converts this into steam power for the lifting mechanism, the Foundry, and general operation. Dwarven Cores (small heat-charged batteries) power individual sentries. Spent cores return to the Core Exchange via pneumatic tubes, get recharged on heating elements, and are sent back out.

**Sentry types:**
- Security Sentries — combat-focused, defend the tower, activate on intruders
- Construction Sentries — large, work the expansion zone, non-hostile unless interfered with
- Hauling Sentries — smaller and faster, move materials between floors via internal lifts, ignore intruders unless physically blocked
- Existing bestiary entries (Decrepit Lichen Sentry, Lichen Shield Warden, Ember Vine Sentinel) are from the Collapsed Tower — related infrastructure but degraded. These sentries are clean and fully operational.

**The Boss — Manufactory Guardian.** The largest golem in the tower. Lives on the Manufactory floor. Does not activate until approached or until production is disturbed. Defeating it and reaching Command is required to unlock the elevator. This is the dungeon's final challenge.

**Elevator activation.** Command floor has levers that control tower systems including the elevator lock. Players must fight from the Entrance through Security, ascend all production floors, defeat the Manufactory Guardian, and reach Command. Then the elevator becomes functional.

**The ore.** The Refinery processes an unfamiliar metal — not iron, not copper. This is a Dwarven alloy component. Identifying it requires knowledge the players don't yet have.

**Zigzag stairs.** Each floor's staircase exits on the opposite side from where it began, forcing players to cross the full width of each room. No shortcuts. Every floor is an encounter space.

**Progressive element.** Each visit the tower is visibly taller and the expansion zone has less gap remaining. If left alone indefinitely, the tower completes its current expansion cycle and may begin another.

<details>
<summary>[ ] Scene</summary>

A hill rises beside the game trail, twice the size of a double wide and a bit taller. The trail passes around it.

</details>

---
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. Near the top, a square opening crusted with lichen, half-hidden by moss. Vines trail down inside. Sunlight reaches the bottom.
    1. **Intuition (2):** The edges aren’t carved — they’re cast. One piece, no seams.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Callouts</summary>

Waist-deep water fills a curved chamber. The walls aren’t stone. Stones set into the ceiling shine like the sun. A chair wrapped in vines sits against the far wall — beside it a table with gems inlaid into the surface in impractical ways. Dense vines riddle the interior, dipping down into the water.

</details>

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. *[Fat Bog Stalker — use standard stat block with +1 wound slot, +1 dice to all damage rolls. Trapped but well-fed and territorial.]*

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. Something sits in the chair. Humanoid, still, wrapped in vines so thick you almost miss it. Not stone — something harder, smoother, with joints at the elbows and knees. A face with no features. One hand rests on the chair’s arm. The other hangs at its side, fingers closed around something.
    1. **Intuition (2):** The make is unfamiliar — not like anything you've worked with before. Different material, different proportions.
    2. **Might (2):** You pry the vines from its hand. Inside: a short metal rod, no longer than a cup, with a seam running its length.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. The rod extends with a twist — a short spear, full-length, solid. Another twist and it collapses back. The metal is the same as the figure’s skin. No rust, no wear.

</details>

A buried Calderan construct — a golem turtle, a mobile forward operating base. The bottom entrance is completely buried. The hatch on top was the emergency exit. The interior was once a command space. Centuries of rain through the open hatch flooded and overgrew it.

The humanoid golem is fully inactive. The collapsible spear is a Calderan relic — functional equipment. The sunstones are Calderan infrastructure. This is the party’s first encounter with Calderan technology as distinct from Dwarven. The golem’s material, the sunstones, and the spear all look and feel different from the Collapsed Tower’s stone-and-metal constructs.

description:
*** *First visited: Expedition #* * [ ] \[ ]
[ ] Scene

The flowers thin out where the ground gets wet and willow trees take over. Ponds sit between the roots, still and dark. In the center of the clearing, a stone the size of an elephant — black, smooth, and shining like it's wet even though it isn't.

[ ] Callouts

The stone dominates the clearing — black and featureless, too smooth to be natural.

Near the tree line, a cleared patch of ground with the remains of a campfire — someone was here.

Fresh cuts in the flowers — a wide trail pressed flat where something big and heavy was dragged west. Human bootprints beside it, many sets.

Scattered around the clearing: three or four crude wooden stakes driven into the soil, each one baited with a bundle of pale mushrooms tied at the top. The ground around them is soft and loosely packed.

\- \[ ] \*\*Visit 2 (Progressive)\*\*
[ ] Scene

You return to the clearing. The stone has changed — a thin crack runs down one side, faint light bleeding through from inside.

\- \[ ] \*\*Visit 3 (Progressive)\*\*
[ ] Scene

The black stone again. The cracks have spread — three or four now, branching across the surface. The light from inside is brighter, warm and amber. You can feel heat from it standing a few feet away.

\- \[ ] \*\*Visit 4 (Progressive)\*\*
[ ] Scene

The clearing feels different. The cracks cover half the stone now and the amber light pulses slowly, like breathing. The nearest pond reflects the glow. The willow trees closest to the stone have new growth — green shoots where there were none.

\- \[ ] \*\*Visit 5 (Progressive)\*\*
[ ] Scene

The stone is more crack than surface. Light pours from every split. The warmth is constant now — the mud around the base has dried and hardened. The willows closest to it are thick with new leaves. Something is waking up inside.

*** * [ ] \[ ]
[ ] Details

  1. Up close the surface is perfectly smooth — no chisel marks, no seams, no texture at all. It reflects your torchlight like polished glass. Cold to the touch.

    1. Intuition (2): Pressing your hand flat against it, you feel a faint vibration deep inside. Not movement — more like a hum too low to hear.

    2. Might (3): You can't scratch it, chip it, or mark it with any tool you have.

\- \[ ] \*\*Approach\*\*
[ ] Details

  1. A fire ring of pond stones, long cold. A lean-to frame with no cover — the branches are cut, not broken. Boot prints in the dried mud, human-sized.

    1. The prints lead north toward the drag marks and south back toward the flowers. Whoever camped here came and went more than once.

    2. Intuition (3): Scratched into one of the fire ring stones — tally marks. Twelve of them, grouped in fours. Someone counted days here.

\- \[ ] \*\*Approach\*\*
[ ] Details

  1. Four stakes spaced wide across the clearing, each about as tall as a man. A bundle of pale mushrooms lashed to the top of each. The smell draws the eye before the stake does.

    1. Intuition (2): Directly in front of each stake, the soil is loose and uneven. Step on it and you'd fall. Pits, freshly dug, covered with leaves and packed moss.

    2. Prowess (2): Clear the cover from one. A sharpened stake at the bottom points up. Deep enough to kill anything that falls in, except something elephant-sized — which would land on its front legs and get stuck.

\- \[ ] \*\*Approach\*\*
[ ] Details

  1. The ponds nearest the stone are warmer than the others. Not hot — comfortable, like water that's been sitting in sunlight.

    1. The warm ponds have different growth in them — pale weeds that don't appear in the cold ponds. Something is thriving here that doesn't grow elsewhere.

    2. Intuition (3): Small shapes moving in the warm water — not fish, something slower. Worth collecting for someone who studies living things.

Twelve tally marks on the fire stones. | *** The Black Stone is a seed — a dormant piece of Caldera's deep infrastructure, slowly reactivating. The cracks and light are not damage; something is growing or waking inside. The warmth it radiates is changing the local ecosystem — the warm ponds are incubating life that doesn't exist elsewhere in the Wetland. The old campsite was made by a previous Riftstone expedition that came this far and turned back. The tally marks are days spent studying the stone. Their notes, if they exist, would be back at the Ferry Landing. The stone cannot be broken, moved, or meaningfully interacted with by the party at this stage. description:
---

*First visited: Expedition #*
- [ ] **Visit 1**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Scene</summary>

Broken stone juts from the earth — too square to be natural, too ruined to be standing. A mudslide has carved a ramp into the ground floor, six feet below the surface. The stone is old and pale, nothing like the dark wood around it.

</details>

<details>
<summary>[ ] Callouts</summary>

The mud ramp slopes down into darkness — wet, slick, and steep.

Something stands near the entrance below. Still, but upright. Not a tree.

</details>
- [ ] **Visit 2**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Scene</summary>

Back at the ruined tower. The mud ramp is a little deeper than last time — rain has widened it. From the top you can see further into the ground floor now. Metal glints on shelves inside.

</details>
- [ ] **Visit 3 (Progressive)**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Scene</summary>

The tower again. A wet trail leads up the mud ramp from below — something heavy dragged itself out of the basement recently. The trail dries and disappears into the undergrowth heading east.

</details>
- [ ] **Visit 4 (Progressive)**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Scene</summary>

You come back to find the wet trail is thicker now — multiple tracks, smaller than the first. Faint croaking echoes from below. The smell of stagnant water is stronger.

</details>
- [ ] **Visit 5 (Progressive)**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Scene</summary>

The croaking is louder. Small shapes hop across the mud ramp — fist-sized, wet, pale. The basement is breeding. Whatever laid eggs down there, they're hatching.

</details>

---
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. At the base of the ramp, something stands motionless — shaped like a person but wrong. Stone and metal, no face, no breath. It doesn't react to your voice. When you step closer, it shifts — not toward you, toward the entrance. It wants you to go inside.
    1. It doesn't attack unless attacked first. If you try to leave it steps aside. If you try to go anywhere but the entrance it blocks the way with its body.
    2. **Intuition (3):** It's not alive. It moves but there's no life behind it — no breathing, no heat, no sound except grinding stone when it shifts.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. Past the sentry: a long room with shelves carved into the walls. Metal crates — most torn open, contents scattered. A few still sealed on the top shelves, out of easy reach.
    1. The open crates hold chunks of dull ore — heavy, dark, metallic. Not iron, not copper. Something else.
    2. **Might (3):** You pull a sealed crate down from the top shelf. Inside: the same ore, but these pieces are wrapped individually in oiled cloth. Preserved on purpose. More valuable than the loose stuff.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. At the back of the storage room, stairs go up and stairs go down. The upward stairs are cracked and missing sections — climbing them means trusting stone that's already failed once. The downward stairs are slick with mud and water.
    1. **Up — Prowess/Reflex (3):** You make it to the second floor. Something waits at the top — another figure like the one below, but this one is broken. Legless, charred black, propped against the wall. It's holding a poleaxe. As you crest the stairs, it raises the weapon.
    2. **Down:** The smell hits before you see anything — stagnant water and something organic. The bottom of the stairs is flooded ankle-deep.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. Flooded stone floor, water up to your shins. Half the room is buried in mud. The walls are covered in something round and wet — clusters of gelatinous spheres, each with a dark spot inside. Hundreds of them.
    1. **Intuition (2):** Something large is in the water. You can't see it — the water is too murky. But the surface ripples near the far wall without wind or current.
    2. *Visit 3+:* Some of the egg clusters are empty — torn open from inside. Small shapes swim in the murky water around your legs.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. Behind the broken figure on the second floor — a door made of metal, set into the stone wall. No handle, no keyhole visible. Heavy. The surface has marks where something tried to force it open and failed.
    1. **Might (4):** It doesn't budge. Whatever opens this, it isn't muscle.
    2. **Intuition (3):** The metal is warm to the touch. Something behind it is generating heat.

</details>

---

*(No connections — dead end)*

---

Pre-Incursion infrastructure — a watchtower and storage depot built by whoever managed Caldera before the Nekr'a. The ore in the crates is an unidentified metal connected to the deeper infrastructure. The sentries are constructs — golems or automatons, not living creatures.

The ground floor sentry is passive — it guides visitors toward the entrance and prevents wandering. The second floor sentry is damaged and hostile — it guards the vault door violently. The vault requires a key, mechanism, or knowledge the party doesn't have yet. The warm metal connects to the same infrastructure as the Black Stone.

The progressive element is the Giant Frog colony in the basement. The eggs are hatching over expeditions — the basement becomes increasingly dangerous as juvenile frogs fill the flooded space. The wet trail in Visit 3 is an adult frog leaving to hunt, establishing the basement as a permanent breeding site. Eventually the ground floor may become contested as juveniles grow.
name: Collapsed Tower

*** *First visited: Expedition #* * [ ] \[ ] **Visit 1**
[ ] Scene

The goblin path ends at the lip of a hole in the ground.

A narrower path picks up again on the far side, curving east around the hole to continue deeper into the forest.

The hole is wide and roughly circular, twelve feet across. Roots dangle from crumbling edges. Thick moss and young saplings grow at the broken rim.

Dark water sits at the bottom, matted with green algae. Daylight drops straight into it.

[ ] Callouts

Crushed bone fragments are scattered around the near lip, half-grown-over with moss.

The algae below shifts in one spot.

A faint draft rises from somewhere near the river bank.

\- \[ ] \*\*Visit 2\*\*
[ ] Scene

(To be written — what's changed since last visit?)

\- \[ ] \*\*Visit 3 (Progressive)\*\*
[ ] Scene

(To be written)

*** * [ ] \[ ] **Approach**
[ ] Details

  1. The edges are loose earth, broken roots, and years of leaf litter.

  2. The drop is about twelve feet to waist-deep water below.

    1. Prowess (2): Descend with rope or grappling hook. Failure means falling into the water.

    2. Intuition (2): The crushed bone pieces at the rim are skull fragments. Small — the size of a goblin's.

    3. Intuition (3): The broken earth fans outward from the rim. The opening was blown from below, not from above.

\- \[ ] \*\*Approach\*\*
[ ] Details

  1. Near the river bank, a thick hanging curtain of wet moss covers a depression in the ground.

  2. Pushing through, a low tunnel opens — just large enough for something the size of a gator to squeeze through.

    1. Intuition (2): The moss is parted in one spot where something big regularly comes and goes.

    2. Prowess (3): Crawl through. The tunnel slopes down and surfaces into the common chamber inside.

\- \[ ] \*\*Approach\*\*
[ ] Details

  1. You land in waist-deep water. The chamber is wide and low. Daylight from the sinkhole lights most of it.

  2. The far walls are fractured outward. Niches are carved into the walls at shoulder height — dozens of them, most shattered on the side nearest the blast.

  3. Wetland plants grow thick here. Ferns, saplings, hanging vines reaching down toward the water. The walls are green with moss and pale fungus.

    1. Broken bedding floats on the algae — rotted reeds, scraps of hide, clumps of matted fur.

    2. Crushed bone fragments are pressed into the silt underfoot. Almost no whole pieces.

    3. Intuition (3): The niches nearest the far wall are obliterated. Whoever was sleeping there died instantly. The pattern of destruction fans out from that spot.

\- \[ ] \*\*Approach\*\*
[ ] Details

  1. A passage leads from the sleeping quarters into a larger room. The water is the same depth. No daylight reaches here — it's dark.

  2. Pale plants grow along the walls, reaching for no light. Thick algae covers the surface.

  3. Stone benches line the walls just below the waterline. A raised stone ring sits submerged at the center, filled with dark sludge.

    1. Prowess (2): Move through the water without slipping on the silt below.

    2. The benches ring the central stone. Everything in the room faces inward toward it.

    3. A large reptilian shape rests at the far end of the chamber, watching the hidden tunnel entrance. See bestiary: Bog Stalker.

\- \[ ] \*\*Approach\*\*
[ ] Details

  1. A larger chamber with a higher ceiling. The water reaches your chest. Total dark outside of torchlight.

  2. Algae blankets the surface completely. A rank smell hangs in the air — rot and wet stone.

  3. A stone platform rises toward the center, half-submerged, worn smooth on top. Water laps against it.

    1. Intuition (2): The surface of the water shifts in several places at once. There's more than one thing in here.

    2. Three large reptilian shapes move in and around the pool. Two patrol the water at different depths. One coils on the submerged platform guarding the clutch.

    3. A clutch of eggs sits in a depression on top of the platform, just below the waterline. The adults strike from below the algae. See bestiary: Bog Stalker.

\- \[ ] \*\*Approach\*\*
[ ] Details

  1. The pool bottom is stone, silted heavily. Rounded shapes lie embedded in the silt — stones and something else.

  2. Visibility is near zero below the algae.

    1. Intuition (3): Searching by touch, you feel a rounded object heavier and denser than the stones around it. Larger than a fist. Warm against your skin, even in the cold water.

    2. Prowess (3) + held breath: Retrieve the bezoar. Failure means surfacing empty-handed or for air, either way alerting anything in the pool.

\- \[ ] \*\*Approach\*\*
[ ] Details

  1. A passage at the back of the spawning pool climbs upward. The water drops away underfoot. The room at the top is dry and dark.

  2. Half-empty. Whatever was once stacked against the walls has been disturbed — things overturned, most of the shelves stripped. A few piles remain.

    1. A heap of scrap iron — bent tools, broken blades, nails, fittings. Roughly seven pounds if carried out.

    2. A small pile of salt cubes still sealed in waxed hide. Fifty cubes, give or take.

    3. Twenty carved bones in a separate pile. Intuition (3): The carvings aren't decoration. They're a script. You don't recognize the language.

    4. A small pouch of deep-red metallic dust, sealed tight. The weight is wrong — heavier than it looks. (Alchemical catalyst. Unknown properties until researched.)

    5. A fifth reptilian patrols between this room and the spawning pool passage. See bestiary: Bog Stalker.

*** | Destination | Biome | Path Type | | --------------- | --------- | ----------- | | The Red Bog | Wetland | Goblin Path | | The Black Stone | Amberwood | Goblin Path | *** Abandoned Mudback tribe site. Built entirely underground near the river bank, concealed so well that the forest floor above showed nothing. The goblin path above ran right over the top of the sleeping quarters. Years ago, an ork warband attacked — explosives blew the ceiling open as a shock-and-awe opener, and they poured in through the hole to slaughter the tribe in their sleep. The orks cherry-picked the most valuable loot and left fast. They never found the hidden entrance. They didn't search the storage room thoroughly — they grabbed what was easy and moved on. Five bog stalkers live here now. The hidden entrance accommodates them. The waist-deep water is ideal habitat. The spawning pool holds their clutch. **Suggested placement:** * 1 in the common chamber (guarding the hidden tunnel entry) * 3 in the spawning pool (one on the platform with the clutch, two swimming) * 1 patrolling the storage room passage Adjust based on how loud the party is on arrival. Central organ of a goblin spawning pool — a mass of slime-origin tissue that accumulates mineral deposits and biological concentration over generations. Dormant when the pool dies with the tribe. Incredibly alchemically powerful once properly researched, but unusable raw. Any goblin tribe will pay heavily for its return — an intact bezoar is a sacred object to them. Selling it to a Riftstone Scholar for research use will create lasting diplomatic problems with every goblin tribe in the region if the Snotlings or Mudbacks find out. Alchemical catalyst. Orks didn't recognize it. Riftstone Scholars will pay well to research it. Unknown properties until studied. Twenty pieces. The script is a written goblin language the party cannot read. Snotling shamans may be able to translate if approached the right way. The party may find other sources over time. * 7 lbs scrap iron — Smith value * 50 salt cubes — direct currency * 20 carved bones — Butcher value as currency, or research value with a translator * 1 pouch blood-red metallic dust — Scholar value, high * 1 spawning pool bezoar — diplomatic object, Scholar value extreme, goblin-return value very high If the party returns the bezoar to the Mudback tribe directly, the Mudbacks become neutral-to-friendly — a major diplomatic shift given current tension. The party cannot do this in Session 3. It requires finding and reaching the Mudbacks alive first. Long-tail story hook.

<details>
<summary>[ ] Scene</summary>

A massive fir dominates a small clearing, its dark green canopy closed tight above. At the base of the trunk, three fist-sized openings sit just off the ground. Five feet up, narrow balconies barely wider than a hand circle the trunk. Nine feet up, higher platforms hold tiny wooden mechanisms mounted on swivels. Three boulders sit partly sunken into the soil at the tree's base. Three shallow channels cut into the earth lead away from them to the north — straight, narrow, and dug deep.

</details>

Voices carry from the clearing ahead. Loud, arguing, human.

The cart comes into view first — heavy-built, wooden, stacked high with meat and hide.

A massive tusked creature stands hitched to the cart. It doesn't move like the other animals you've seen. It watches you.

Six armed figures are scattered around the clearing. Some sort cuts from the cart. Others cluster near the boulders in the middle of a shouting match. At the center of the argument, a man with a bow slung across his back.

A heavy-set goblinoid stands close to the hitched beast. Quiet. Watching everything.

The hitched beast's eyes follow you. The other animals in sight do not.

Fragments of the argument reach you — something about tracks, about turning back, about a kill that got away.

The goblinoid is armed but hasn't raised a weapon.

<summary>[ ] Scene</summary>

The goblin path winds through thick wetland foliage.

A sweet, rotting smell rises up ahead. Stronger the closer you get.

The undergrowth here is dense — ferns, vines, waist-high reeds — pressing in on both sides of the path.

</details>

<details>
<summary>[ ] Callouts</summary>

The smell is sweet and organic, not sulfuric.

The foliage ahead rustles in places where there is no wind.

No insects. No birds. No sound of small life.

</details>
- [ ] **Visit 2**

---
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. As the party moves through the thick foliage, something wet and rope-thick lashes out from the undergrowth.
2. Tendrils reach through the vegetation, grabbing at ankles and wrists, trying to drag the nearest body toward whatever's on the other side.
    1. **Prowess/Might (4):** Resist being grabbed.
    2. **Prowess/Might (4):** Tear free once grabbed. Slashing weapons effective. Blunt useless.
    3. *See bestiary: Blood Snatcher. Multiple tendrils may grab simultaneously.*

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. Past the foliage, the pool opens up. Larger than any other pool in this region.
2. The water is blood red and murky. The surface does not steam. It barely moves.
3. The tendrils withdraw back into the water in coordinated motion as you watch.
    1. **Intuition (2):** Nothing is visible beneath the surface. The water is too dark and too thick.
    2. **Intuition (3):** The sweet smell is strongest right at the water's edge. Concentrated organic decomposition.
    3. *See bestiary: Blood Snatcher. 50 Endurance. Resistant to Bludgeoning. Weak to Slashing.*

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. With the plant dead, the water settles. Tendrils go limp and sink.
2. Wading in, the pool floor comes into reach. Silt and bones everywhere.
3. Harvesting is straightforward but slow. There is a lot to carry out.
    1. **70 bones.** The tendrils stripped everything clean. Standard trade currency.
    2. **8 goblin skulls.** Intact, separate from the broken bones. Valuable trade with any goblin tribe.
    3. **8 doses of hemotoxic poison.** Recovered from the goblin weapons and gear tangled in the remains. Weapon coating — changes weapon damage type to Hemotoxic.
    4. **Root hearts** from the dead plant, still embedded in the silt at the center. Cooked, they heal minor wounds during rest. Tinctured, the consumer gains 2d4 Endurance at the start of each turn for the rest of combat.

</details>

---

| Destination | Biome | Path Type | 
| --- | --- | --- | 
| The Black Stone | Amberwood | Goblin Path | 
| Young Amber Fir Field | Amberwood | Goblin Path | 
| Beached Corpse | Wetland | Goblin Path | 

---

A pool overgrown with a mature Blood Snatcher — the fully-lethal end stage where the entire water surface is unsafe.

The pool has been killing for a long time. 70 bones stripped clean across the floor. A goblin raiding party (likely Mudback) wandered in recently and joined the pile, but they're just the most recent victims. Their 8 skulls are intact because they sank fast enough that the tendrils didn't reach them fully before the silt covered them.

The Blood Snatcher is the entire encounter. It tries to grab through the foliage *before* the party sees the pool — this is its ambush window. Once past that, it grabs anyone entering the water.

**Key tactics:**
- Slashing weapons mandatory. Bludgeoning is useless.
- Players cannot fight it from the water safely — tendrils will pull them under.
- Best approach: attack from shore, force it to over-commit tendrils, sever them as they reach.
- **70 bones** — standard Butcher trade currency
- **8 goblin skulls** — valuable trade object with any goblin tribe
- **8 doses hemotoxic poison** — weapon coating, changes weapon damage to Hemotoxic
- **Blood Snatcher Root Hearts** — healing resource

Once the plant is dead, harvesting is trivial but time-consuming. The pool floor is thoroughly silted. Recovering everything is a commitment — this is not a smash-and-grab location.

description:
---

*First visited: Expedition #*
- [ ] **Visit 1**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Scene</summary>

A crack in the ground, wide enough to walk through, walls slick with black mold. The air coming out of it is warm, wet, and smells like something dead. The mold thickens deeper in.

</details>

<details>
<summary>[ ] Callouts</summary>

The walls are close enough to touch both sides at once — the passage narrows as it goes deeper. Scratch marks on the stone at waist height.

Bones scattered on the ground near the entrance — small, cracked, picked clean.

</details>
- [ ] **Visit 2**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Scene</summary>

The crevasse again. The bones near the entrance are different — fresher, larger. Something bigger died here since your last visit. The scratch marks on the walls go deeper than you noticed before.

</details>
- [ ] **Visit 3 (Progressive)**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Scene</summary>

You come back and the mold has spread — the entrance stones that were clean before are now black and slick. Musky scent markings layer over the death smell. Something is claiming this place more aggressively.

</details>
- [ ] **Visit 4 (Progressive)**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Scene</summary>

The crevasse entrance has drag marks now — something heavy was pulled inside recently. The musky smell is stronger and there's a new sound deeper in — low cackling, echoing off the wet walls.

</details>
- [ ] **Visit 5 (Progressive)**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Scene</summary>

The cackling is constant now. The bones at the entrance are piled, not scattered — arranged into a rough barrier. Whatever lives deeper inside is fortifying outward. The death smell is overwhelming.

</details>

---
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. The walls are coated in black growth — wet to the touch, it comes off on your hands and clothes. The floor is slippery. The passage slopes downward and the air gets warmer.
    1. **Fortitude (2):** The mold irritates your lungs after prolonged exposure. Covering your mouth helps. Failure means coughing — loud, echoing, announces your presence deeper in.
    2. **Intuition (2):** The scratch marks on the walls are at two different heights — a set at your waist and a set near the floor. Two different things use this passage.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. The passage opens into a wider space where the walls pull apart. The floor is littered with bones, torn hide, and fur. The cackling is louder here — echoing from tunnels on both sides.
    1. **Coin flip:** Cacklers present or not. If present: 3-4 males in the chamber, alert, circling. They know this space better than you and the footing is terrible.
    2. **Intuition (3):** The bones on the floor include ribs the size of ox ribs and horned skulls. Whatever hunts here drags large prey underground to eat.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. Beyond the kill chamber the passage widens again. Something large fills the space — the size of a cart ox, but wrong. It's standing on four legs in the dark but it isn't breathing. Torchlight catches metal and wood where there should be hide and bone.
    1. It does not react to light or sound. It reacts to movement within arm's reach. Then it moves — fast, mechanical, wrong.
    2. **Intuition (2):** This thing is built from a tusked grazer's corpse. Wood and metal threaded through dead muscle. Someone made this. It guards what's behind it.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. Past the dead machine: a chamber large enough to hold the thing that guards it. The walls are lined with small structures carved into the stone — doorways barely big enough to crawl through, shelves of tiny tools, a workbench at ground level stained with dark fluids.
    1. The workbench has restraints. Bone clamps, leather straps, channels for draining fluids. Whatever was built out front was built in here.
    2. **Intellect (3):** The tools are surgical — tiny scalpels, probes, syringes made from bone. Whoever worked here was precise, methodical, and doing something to dead animals that involved putting new things inside them.

</details>

---

| Destination | Biome | Path Type | 
| --- | --- | --- | 
| The Bone Field | Deep Amber | Cattlepos Trail | 

---

A corrupted Nekr'a workshop. The small structures are Nekr'a living quarters. The workbench is where they built Nekromechs — dead animals reanimated with mechanical components. The Cattlepos Nekromech guards the workshop autonomously, still following its last orders.

The Cacklers are secondary occupants — they moved into the kill chamber because it's defensible and close to the surface for hunting. They avoid the Nekromech. The progressive element shows the Cackler pack consolidating: more kills dragged inside, territorial markings expanding, eventually bone fortifications at the entrance. The Cacklers and the Nekromech coexist by avoiding each other — the Cacklers stay in the upper chambers, the machine stays deeper.

The surgical tools and the Nekromech itself are the party's first direct evidence that the Nekr'a did more than forestry — they built things from dead animals. This is a dark discovery that recontextualizes every Nekr'a site they've visited. The tools connect to the Nekr'a corruption arc.

**This location is a dead end.** It needs a second connection to avoid backtracking — consider linking it to another Dry Caverns location when one is developed nearby.

<details>
<summary>[ ] Scene</summary>

The valley wall rises ahead. A palisade made from bones tied together by razor-sharp vines blocks the path. A field of massive yellow ferns covers the ground in front of it. Snotlings open the gate and welcome you in — always with at least six armed snotlings guiding you.

Batkin Sulfur Outpost. This sinkhole is a stranded mining colony belonging to the Batkin. The outpost mines sulfur from the sinkhole's geothermal deposits and processes guano into saltpeter. Combined with charcoal from fallen trees, these are the three ingredients for gunpowder — the Batkin's primary military advantage.

Cut off. The caved-in tunnel was their supply line back to the main Batkin territory. The Mudback goblins collapsed it intentionally, severing this outpost. The Batkin cannot call for reinforcements or ship their gunpowder stockpile out.

Undead as passive defense. Batkin don't clear undead — they roost high where the zombies can't reach. The corpse sea on the cave floor was once a much larger horde. Cut off from resupply, most have fully rotted. Only 6 functional walkers remain at the work stations, plus crawlers hidden in the corpse piles and shamblers stumbling through the mess. Zombie composition: Ork Zombies and Mudback Goblin Zombies. The goblin zombies are notably old — Mudback goblins normally take their dead back to the spawning pool before mycelial conversion, so their skulls stay alive long after death and bodies take much longer to turn.

The bat town. Three adobe domes on the cave ceiling. The Production Dome is largest and where the hoist arrives — full of gunpowder processing vats. The Sleeping Dome and Food Storage Dome are on the far side, each guarded by a mounted gun outside the door. The food vats are filled with blood. 3 Vampiric Bats remain alive. 3 Stalker Bats roost here at night, 6 during the day, hanging from the metal rods between domes. All dome interiors are difficult terrain from storage clutter.

Armaments:

Mounted Gun (×3): 30m range, 2AP fire, 3AP reload, 3d12+Prowess Shrapnel. One at hoist top, one outside each far dome.

Batkin Bomb: 2AP throw, 4d4+4 Shrapnel, 3m radius. Stockpiled in the equipment dome.

Batkin rifles and bone armor also stored in the equipment dome.

Day vs Night. During the day, 6 Stalker Bats roost in the cave. The cave is deafeningly loud with clicking and flapping. At night, most bats leave to hunt — only 3 Stalker Bats and the 3 Vampiric Bats remain. Night entry is quieter but the Batkin are home and alert.

Snotling Quest Connection. The Snotling Tribe wants the Batkin dealt with — they've been raiding goblin territory. Completing this is a major snotling alliance quest payoff.

Sulfur. The yellow crystals are sulfur, mined from geothermal deposits around the still water. The white crystals in the evaporation pans are saltpeter refined from guano. Both are valuable — sulfur especially so as a gunpowder component.

Player choices. Kill the Batkin (snotling quest), trade with them (they're desperate and cut off), or ignore them and loot the sulfur. Clearing the cave also removes the undead threat from this hex.

---

*First visited: Expedition #*
- [ ] **Visit 1 — Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Scene</summary>

Through the trees ahead, something solid runs across the forest floor — trunks grown so tight together they touch, and boulders jammed into the gaps between them. A wall, made of living wood and stone, ringing something you can't yet see.

</details>

<details>
<summary>[ ] Callouts</summary>

The wall runs in both directions until the trees swallow the line of sight.

One gap breaks the wall — a narrow opening between two of the trunks, just wide enough for a person.

</details>
- [ ] **Visit 1 — Inside the Clearing**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Scene</summary>

Through the gap, the walled space opens into a round clearing. A massive fir stands at the center, its dark green canopy closed tight above. At the base of its trunk, three fist-sized openings sit just off the ground. Five feet up, narrow balconies barely wider than a hand circle the trunk. Nine feet up, higher platforms hold wooden mechanisms the length of a forearm — bigger than hand-sized, but still Nekr'a-scale. Long stone basins sit at ground level between the roots, stained dark amber inside. A musky stink rises from a gap between the roots on the north side of the trunk.

</details>

<details>
<summary>[ ] Callouts</summary>

The mechanisms on the upper platforms are bigger than those at the other hovel — forearm-sized, not hand-sized.

The stone basins are stained in patterns that look worn-in, not spilled.

The musky stink at the base of the tree is strong enough to make your eyes water up close.

</details>
- [ ] **Visit 2**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Scene</summary>

Back at the walled clearing. The hovel tree looks the same, but the silence is different — no insect noise from the canopy, no bird calls. Something new has moved in above.

</details>
- [ ] **Visit 3 (Progressive)**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Scene</summary>

The clearing again. One of the stone basins has fresh residue crusted on the inside — still wet in places. Something has been using the basins recently.

</details>
- [ ] **Visit 4 (Progressive)**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Scene</summary>

The hovel tree has new growth — pale threads hanging from the lowest branches on the north side, straighter than lichen and not moving right in the wind.

</details>
- [ ] **Visit 5 (Progressive)**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Scene</summary>

The threads have spread. Tiny amber shapes drift down from the canopy like slow glowing snow. Some land on the stone basins below.

</details>

---
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. Walking the perimeter from outside, the trees didn't grow this way on their own. The trunks are deliberately tight — roots interwoven, bark grown around bark. Boulders have been wedged between where gaps remained, and moss has grown over them. Only the single entrance breaks the wall.
    1. **Intuition (3):** This is a defensive perimeter. The wall was shaped — trees guided as they grew, stones moved in by many hands over a long time.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. Up close the fist-sized openings at the base lead into tiny hollow chambers inside the trunk — no bigger than your fist. Carved shelves no wider than a fingernail line the walls, most empty. At five feet up, the balconies circle the trunk — barely a handspan wide, worn and polished in places by generations of tiny feet. The trunk has shallow handholds shaped into the bark to climb between levels, each one sized for a creature the size of a large squirrel.
    1. **Intuition (2):** The scale is all wrong for a person. Everything here was built for something smaller than a human fist.
    2. Reaching into one of the fist-sized openings, your hand doesn't fit. A finger might, but only just.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. Nine feet up, platforms hold wooden mechanisms mounted on swivels. Each is about as long as a forearm, with a loaded bolt the length of a finger. Four of them, spaced around the trunk. Frames cracked with age, cords rotted through, but the working parts are intact.
    1. **Intuition (2):** These are arbalists — the largest class of siege weapon at their scale. The mechanisms at the other hovel were hand-crossbow-sized; these are the next tier up.
    2. **Might (2):** Pry one loose. Light enough to carry in one hand. A skilled artificer could rebuild it into a human-scale arbalist, or use the parts as-is for a hand crossbow.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. Three long stone troughs at ground level between the roots of the hovel tree. Stained dark amber inside. One has hardened residue crusted in the corners.
    1. The residue smells sharp and chemical — nothing like the raw amber on the trees.
    2. **Might (3):** Pry out a chunk of the hardened stuff. Solid, smooth, and warm to the touch. Worth something to someone who works with materials.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. At the north side of the hovel tree's base, a gap opens downward between the roots. The smell is animal and rotten underneath. Gnawed bones ring the opening, and a foul patch of churned ground sits just outside it — droppings and bone scraps and scraps of hide, thick with flies.
    1. The gap leads into a passage dug through roots and soil. It drops at an angle, just wide enough for a medium creature to pass through.
    2. **Intuition (2):** The fouled patch at the entrance is a latrine. The smell is meant to warn things away from what's below.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. One tree at the south edge of the wall has a root that rises high enough to stand on. From the top, the full clearing is visible — the hovel tree at the center, basins ringing its base, the wall running unbroken except for the single gap.
    1. To the northeast, a gap in the canopy far in the distance. To the west, older growth.

</details>

Nekr'a forestry and refining outpost. The hovel tree is an Old Verdant Fir shaped to house workers — the doors, balconies, and upper platforms are all built to Nekr'a scale. The upper platforms here mount arbalist-scale mechanisms — the largest class of Nekr'a siege weapons — rather than the hand-crossbow-sized mechanisms at other outposts. This was a defensive position as well as a productive one. The stone basins refined amber resin into alchemical compounds. The walled perimeter with its single entrance confirms this was a controlled, guarded site. Only one way in, one way out.

A Cackler pack has taken the root passages below. The musky gap is their entrance and exit. The latrine at the mouth is deliberate — warning other predators off. The pack is actively established — the Canopy Clutch colony spreading in the canopy is the secondary consequence of nature reclaiming the refinery with no one managing it.

*See bestiary: *[*Cacklers*](hexicon://notion-page/341e50e3-bf79-81c2-b7e4-f1359cbad17b)*, *[*Cackler Matriarch*](hexicon://notion-page/341e50e3-bf79-817c-9a97-e40673646c81)*. See location: *[*The Cackler Lair*](hexicon://location/40)*.*

A huge weeping vine oasis in the Deep Amber — significantly larger than a typical oasis. Three live Oasis Maws colonize the vine wall at roughly even spacing around the perimeter. A fourth Oasis Maw died long enough ago that its leaked digestive fluid has tinted the pool brown and left a faint salty taste in the air and water.

A small Howler family of five adults is settling into the high canopy above. New arrivals — minimal rock caches, no pups yet.

The three live Maws are the core encounter. Each is a standard Oasis Maw fight on its own. Three of them means the oasis is a layered gauntlet — a party that blunders in wet-footed will have all three Maws tracking their position simultaneously through electroreception, even if only one has grabbed so far.

The Howlers are not a forced encounter. Defensive only — five adults, easily avoided by not provoking them. Triggers: climbing their trees, lingering in the canopy's drop zone, prolonged combat below.

The fourth pitcher plant in the vine wall is dead and safe. Clear visual tell: limp colorless vines, cracked pitcher. A party that identifies it first gets a combat-free harvest and a template for reading the live three.

Brackish, brown-tinted, faintly salty from the dead Maw's leaked digestive fluid. No mechanical effect.

- **Howlers** — only if triggered and killed. Standard Howler harvest.
- Splitting weapons (axes) mandatory for the Maws. Slashing tough, bludgeoning useless.
- Electroreception means wet ground = detection. Dry approaches on roots or rocks avoid this.
- A party that identifies the dead pitcher first gets a safer first harvest and a template for reading the others.

<summary>[ ] Scene</summary>

A herd of bristly hogs has settled the field — rooting through the ferns, sleeping in wallows they've dug in the soil. They watch you with small dark eyes but don't scatter. Something larger tracks the edge of the field at dusk now, drawn by the herd.

</details>

---
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. Up close the bark is smoother and lighter than other amber firs. The golden lumps are hard and warm to the touch — resin, solidified over years. Some are cracked where they've dried.
    1. The lumps break off cleanly with a knife or chisel. Each one is palm-sized and heavy for its size.
    2. **Might (2):** You can pry off 3-4 lumps before they get harder to reach. Worth good salt to anyone who works with materials.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. Parting the ferns carefully: small burrows in the soil between the roots. Something has been digging — turned earth, chewed stems, tiny tracks.
    1. **Intuition (2):** The tracks are rodent-sized, not dangerous. The digging has exposed fat tubers in the soil — the ferns grow from bulbs. That's what the animals are eating.
    2. The bulbs are edible. Enough here to supplement rations for a day's travel.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. A stake the height of a man, driven deep into the soil. Rope tied at the top and cut off crudely — the cut edge is frayed, not sliced clean. The ground around the post is churned up where something huge thrashed and then moved on.
    1. **Intuition (2):** The rope was tied to something at the top that's now gone. Whatever it was, it drew something that could pull that hard.
    2. The trail from the post leads northwest, deep and wide. Something heavy was walking, not being dragged.

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. A pit about twice the width of a man, dug into the soil between stands of ferns. Bait stake broken flat next to it.
2. Inside the pit, both front legs of a massive tusked creature are wedged down into the earth. It's halfway in, hindquarters still on solid ground, unable to lift itself out.
3. It roars when you get close, heaves, and throws soil into the air. It's bleeding from the shoulder where it scraped against something going down.
    1. The bottom of the pit is lined with sharpened stakes. Two are broken where the front hooves drove through them. The creature takes slow damage from them every time it shifts.
    2. Killing it is trivial from outside the pit. Freeing it is a Might/Prowess challenge and a time risk — and it will not be grateful.
    3. Walking past it means leaving a suffering animal to rise within hours if it dies and isn't processed.

*See bestiary: *[*Cattlepos*](hexicon://notion-page/341e50e3-bf79-810d-99d5-eba7b4a45524)*, *[*Mycelial Undead*](hexicon://notion-page/345e50e3-bf79-8118-a57e-f281a0607e4f)*.*

</details>
- [ ] **Approach**

<details>
<summary>[ ] Details</summary>

1. *Visit 5+:* Large prints circle the field's edge in the soft soil. Clawed, heavy, spaced like something that walks on four legs. Fresh.
    1. **Intuition (3):** The tracks circle but never enter the field. Whatever it is, it's watching the herd from the tree line, waiting for one to stray.

</details>

A natural amber deposit — the pale tree produces higher-quality resin than normal amber firs. The progressive element is a Pygmy Hog herd establishing a permanent feeding ground here, drawn by the tuber-rich soil. Their presence eventually attracts a Cackler pack or similar predator to the field edges. The players can harvest amber freely on early visits but later visits mean navigating around a herd and its predators. The amber regrows slowly — lumps return over many expeditions if the tree isn't killed.

---

The Verdant Watch Cackler pack. Linear layout: descent → Bone Room → Meat Store → Matriarch's Chamber. Single main passage, sized for the matriarch. Humans crouch or squeeze. No junctions or branching corridors.

Small flee-holes branch off the main passage throughout the lair. Cackler-sized only — they form a hidden network the pack uses to ambush intruders and retreat between attacks. Expect males to appear from any direction, strike, and disappear.

The ammonia meat-preservation behavior is unique to this pack. Acidic urine denatures flesh-borne bacteria and masks the scent from aerial scavengers.

The latrine sits outside the entrance (at the Verdant Watch clearing) to keep the lair itself clean while using the smell as a territorial warning.

**Pack dispositions:**
- Matriarch + pups both die → pack scatters, lair abandoned within days.
- Matriarch dies, pups survive → males will try to raise them and fail.
- Matriarch lives → pack holds the Verdant Watch indefinitely.

**Combat notes:** Main passage is single-file for humans. Polearms and heavy weapons useless. Light weapons and Prowess-based fighters have the advantage. Flee-holes are the real combat threat — males enter and exit the fight at will through them. Fire works but risks smoldering roots.
name: The Cackler Lair

The expedition hub on the far bank from Riftstone. Deliberately temporary — the palisade, tents, and tarp-covered smithy are all built for quick relocation as the colony pushes deeper into the caldera. The cleared dirt inside the perimeter is because the soil here is too recently turned for anything to grow back.

Four service nodes cover the full expedition economy:

**Physician's Tent** — treatment, medical hires for expeditions

**Butcher's Hut** — bounties in salt cubes and iron keys, Survivalist hires, kill-location flags for large creatures

**Smith's Tarp** — gear repair, squire and porter hires

**The Stone Structure** — map data purchase, Scholar hires (paid on survival, not contract)

The Stone Structure itself is pre-Riftstone — the same make as the Black Stone, and from its top the Collapsed Tower is visible far to the west. The party may not connect these dots early.

The Ferry Landing is where expeditions begin and end. PCs return between expeditions for rest, healing, bounties, trade, and news.
